utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, perhaps I can address you. The position, as you know, is that Judge Robinson is not here this morning. The reason is that his wife is in hospital expecting an operation. It had been thought that it would be today, but there is now some doubt about that. The upshot is that he will not be here and may not be here tomorrow and the day after. We are in a position, if everybody is agreeable, to certainly finish this witness, which would be desirable, with only two of us, taking depositions under Rule 71. Now, I hope the parties have had notice of the position, have had a chance of considering it. As far as the Prosecution is concerned, is there any objection to that course?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: As to completing the direct, the cross, and the redirect of witness Michael Buffini, there is no objection. We have, in fact, during the break, prepared the application that is necessary under the Kupreskic holdings. It was our understanding that it might be a joint one; I have been informed by Hunton & Williams that they will simply not oppose ours. I am not clear at this point of the position of Mr. Kovacic; however, application will be filed, and no objection as to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It requires an application of only one party, so that will be sufficient. Yes, now, what about any other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: First I have to express regret that at this time Mr. Nice is not available, because of the very late arrival of the next witness, and I have been asked to convey that he would like to have an opportunity to consider whether or not it would be appropriate with the following witnesses to proceed by deposition. Perhaps, if the Court would grant us, after Mr. Buffini's testimony, a break, he would be in a better position to inform the Court of his assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. He, of course, can address us on it. But we can go on, then, until the break, which will be at half past 11, and perhaps he can deal with the matter then. Mr. Sayers, is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Your Honour, and I believe a written notice of nonobjection has been faxed to the legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Same with us, Your Honour. No objection on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, as you have just said, if I have understood you correctly, you are presenting a written request which is being presented pursuant to Rule 71(B); that is, a motion which indicates the name of the individual who is to be examined, the date, and the place, so that we be in accordance with Sub-rule 71(B). Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sorry. The application has been submitted, I believe, to the Registrar, and I believe the date is -- all the necessary points are in there, and we would be so prepared to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Judge Bennouna reminds me it is the case that we have consulted Judge Robinson on the telephone about this matter, and it's the decision of the Trial Chamber that we should proceed by deposition. We'll go on with this witness. Mr. Buffini, I'm sorry you've been kept waiting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, yesterday, although I apologise because I did not have the benefit of a transcript to review the point from which I had left off, but going back to yesterday, you were indicating that there had been a discussion and complaint raised about the use by the HVO of Muslim either civilians and/or prisoners of war for trench digging and for human shields. This was pursued, and --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you, in fact, shown any of the areas where the alleged trench digging and/or human shield activity was to have taken place, and if so, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not taken and shown the areas, but we were given the locations where the incidents were supposed to have happened. We then went directly to those locations to view for ourselves, and all we saw were freshly dug trenches which had been done within 24 hours or so of our visit, but we saw no prisoners and no civilians in the area at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you seek permission to go there, or any intervention and assistance by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we actually asked Mr. Cerkez if he would take us to the locations so that we could check the complaint ourselves; this is Henk Morsink and I. But after a general discussion, we weren't escorted. We visited the location ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you detect any delay in your having access to said sites?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very clear that it was a time-delaying tactic, because we insisted on moving there as quickly as possible but then got embroiled in a discussion about burning houses and other incidents that were happening to HVO and Bosnian Croat troops at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Without spending unnecessary time in any repetition of videos, as indicated yesterday, I would ask that the third clip of the video which was presented during prior testimony of Mr. Morsink be shown to the Court, and as indicated yesterday, I would request that the entire video, which has been submitted to the Defence, be submitted to the Court so that should the Chamber wish to view it in its entirety, it can have it at its disposal. At this time we would ask the audio people to help out with that third clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, before that happens, Mr. Kovacic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to raise a minor matter, that is the video we have seen on which I have objection that the translation is not correct. You ordered at that time that we should get an accurate translation. We still haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Right. That's something we need to look into. Now let's play the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Yes, but they said in the other part. In which part? He said that it was near the place where the mines were placed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, the video which you have seen, if you could comment on who the individuals are who perhaps are not known to the Court, and if you could indicate what the structure -- it appeared to be grey brick-like in a field -- was just prior to the British gentleman speaking was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The characters involved, though, Henk Morsink and another ECMM person was involved with our translator. We'd also brought along one of the HVO troops who had been sent by Mr. Cerkez to identify the location of the burning house, but he obviously couldn't pinpoint the exact location. And we saw nothing anywhere in about an hour's driving around to indicate that any houses had been set on fire or were burning. In the video you saw an anti-personnel mine which was in the grass, which had had a trip wire attached to it, so that people walking around that area, if they weren't careful, could easily have detonated that anti-personnel mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who was the British gentleman who began to comment about the absence of burning houses?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman in the blue flak jacket was Geoffrey Archer who at the time was a news correspondent for the ITN news in the United Kingdom. He's now an author of some books.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was the HVO representative who was with you and who was in that video also present when Mr. Cerkez gave the description of where the houses should be found?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He had joined in the conversation with Henk Morsink and myself and had been given the location to investigate by Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did that HVO representative ride in the same vehicle with you to the locations?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He was in the same vehicle as us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there a meeting at the end of April in 1993 at which Ambassador Jean-Pierre Thebault from ECMM attended and also General Petkovic and General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that meeting was held in the ECMM house in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you present?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was for most of the meeting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who from the representative level of the HVO and the ABiH were present, the local level rather?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the local level we had our normal representatives of Mr. Merdan, Mr. Nakic, and I believe other commanders from the area there, including Mr. Cerkez, and I don't believe Colonel Blaskic was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was this after Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was definitely after Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What, if anything, was agreed upon at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting agreed that there would be a Central Bosnia-wide ceasefire which would take effect that evening. There would also be an exchange of lists of prisoners and close co-operation with the ICRC about prisoner releases. And there was also an agreement that troops on front-line positions would move back to designated positions which were given behind their own front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Based on your experience on the joint commission, did you make any -- come to any conclusions about the degree of authority that Mario Cerkez exhibited as opposed to the degree of authority which Franjo Nakic exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was very clear that Mr. Nakic had very little authority when asked to make decisions agreed by the joint commission, whereas we felt that Mr. Cerkez had far more authority in deciding something. When he actually said that something would be done, we knew that that would be achieved.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you learn of the holding of 60 or so Bosnian Muslim males in the Vitez cinema by the HVO at some point?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were actually taken there with General Petkovic and General Halilovic during the tour of the Stari Vitez, Vitez area. And I personally went into the cinema with the group who were escorting the two Generals and saw the 60 odd prisoners in the cinema.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate the ages of the individuals?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ages of most of them were over 30 to 55. There were very few, if at all, young people under the age of 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And these were males?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were always males.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did their release come about?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The release was given when we attended, so that both Generals agreed that all the prisoners were free to go as of that moment, and were able to walk out of the cinema, should they choose to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did any or all of these individuals, to your knowledge, express a fear about their safety at the hands of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there were only six people who felt confident enough to leave at that time. All the others feared that as soon as they left the cinema, they would either be shot or attacked by HVO troops in the local area. So they actually stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did they set any conditions for their leaving the cinema?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prisoners that were held specifically requested protection from UNPROFOR troops before they moved out. So they wanted escorting from the location.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did they receive it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that point, no. We couldn't provide them at that time with that support.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a feature known as Maklen ridge?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd ask -- excuse me. I'd ask the usher to distribute Z22612,7. Mr. Buffini, looking at the map before you, are you able to point to the location of Maklen?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maklen was just north of Prozor. It went up the steep hill. At the top of the hill was Maklen ridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Does the Chamber have a video of it? Okay. That's fine. Thank you. Ours just came on. What was the significance, if you know, of this particular feature?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance that we were informed of was that this was more or less a front-line position, which was a natural feature between Prozor in the south and Gornji Vakuf in the north and was a dominating position for the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you completed your tour in Bosnia, what did you then do? Excuse me. Before you answer that. When you finished your tour in covering the matters which have been the subject of this examination, did you then work in the Sarajevo area and other areas in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once the joint commission had moved to Travnik, where the BiH Army and HVO army had set up a joint headquarters, my job ceased to function and I deployed my troops to different locations, and used to visit those to investigate the type of roles they would be deployed in. So we went to Maglaj, we went to Sarajevo, Zadar and a few other places as well, even including Dubrovnik and Prevlaka.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did you leave Bosnia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I finally left on the 12th of July, I think it was, that I flew out of Split back to the United Kingdom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Buffini. My name is Steven Sayers. Together with my colleague, Mr. Naumovski, we represent the accused Dario Kordic. The gentlemen over to my left here, Mr. Kovacic and Mr. Mikulicic, they represent Mr. Cerkez. I do not think that the questions that I have for you will take particularly long, sir. There are three areas that I would like to concentrate upon. First, your duties as the chief intelligence -- military intelligence officer in the area and the liaison officers who were working with you. Second, the chain of command issues that you addressed in your direct testimony. And third, the issue relating to the HV troops that you say you saw in the area of Prozor and areas to the south of that in the spring of 1993. And I'll try to make it clear which area I am questioning you about so that we all know where we are going. As I understand it, Mr. Buffini, you were actually the officer in charge of the United Kingdom liaison offices, the UKLO's in the area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the primary task of the UKLO's, or one of the primary tasks, correct me if I'm wrong, is or was the gathering of military intelligence relating to certain specific subjects that you were tasked to investigate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. It wasn't specific gathering of military intelligence. It was gathering information about activities along the main supply routes and other areas where British and United Nations troops were working to ensure that we were forewarned of any difficulties or any problems that would impede our tasks with the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I stand duly corrected. Basically, what you were doing was gathering all kinds of intelligence that would effect the mission of UNPROFOR, if you like, and British and other forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the provision of humanitarian aid to needy persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was gathering that type of information for those purposes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thanks. You actually worked for an entity with the acronym of "ComBritFor" from January the 15th, 1993, to July the 12th, 1993. I think you've testified to that. Could you just elucidate what ComBritFor actually was, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "ComBritFor" was the title for "Commander, British Forces," which was deployed in Divulje barracks and had the responsibility for support to the British Battalion and other United Nations agencies working through Croatia into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the head of ComBritFor, I think that you testified to this, was Brigadier Andrew Cumming, based in Split, Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the first of the two brigadiers I served under, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the second one was? That's okay. And you were detached to the Busovaca area at the beginning of February 1993, I believe, was your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the end of February, beginning of March. I think it was March the 3rd I moved up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There were two officers under your command, specifically two LOs, Captain Tom Major and Captain Mike Robison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and they deployed to the Busovaca joint commission in early February, mid-February, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Their role was to advise the European Community Monitoring Mission on security matters and to act as a communications link with you in ComBritFor via their satellite telephones and radios; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite. The communication was really to provide links with the British Battalion for any immediate support, and also back to UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak, as well as to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be fair to say that you were in fairly constant communication with your liaison officers, and through them, with BritBat?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in daily contact most of the time with the U.K. liaison officers, and occasionally had the need to liaise with BritBat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: When you were actually deployed into the area of Central Bosnia, sir, you obviously had personal contact with the military information offices for the two British battalions whose presence in the area your tour of duty straddled; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We went to the daily briefings which both battalions had in an evening, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That would be captain Chris Leighton for the Cheshire Regiment and Captain Simon Harrison for the 1st Battalion of the Prince of Wales Own Regiment of Yorkshire; correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were both the -- the officers involved, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you've previously given a statement to the investigators for the Prosecution, I believe, dated April the 2nd and 3rd, 1997, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain of that. I don't relate to which document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, do you remember actually giving a written statement which you signed -- the date, I'll represent to you, is April the 2nd and 3rd, 1997, but the date that you signed it was actually April the 4th, 1997?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And you testified, I believe, sir, in the Blaskic case on December the 17th of 1997?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One issue that I was interested in in your statement was you were involved in some heated discussions between General Morillon and ComBritFor regarding who actually had command and control over the BritBat component of UNPROFOR; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a phone call from General Morillon to get Brigadier Cumming on the phone, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who did have control over BritBat? Was it UNPROFOR, or was it ComBritFor?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNPROFOR had direct control, and they had command of BritBat in the territory that they were working in. ComBritFor provided the military support for that battalion and did not have direct command of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning very briefly to the situation that you found when you travelled to Central Bosnia in the early part of 1993, Mr. Buffini, there is no question that you found a series of geographically isolated Bosnian Croat enclaves essentially surrounded by ABiH forces; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain areas; I'm not certain that they were enclaves. But, yes, certain Bosnian Croat areas with BiH army surrounding most of those places, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just two specific questions on these. There is no question that the Bosnian Croats controlled the area between Vitez and Busovaca, but there is equally no question that from Kacuni to Bilalovac, which are two villages just to the south of Busovaca, that was area controlled by ABiH forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That essentially cut off the main supply route between the town of Kiseljak to the south and Busovaca to the north; right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The second question is, you gave some testimony relating to the route triangle in the area of Prozor and Gornji Vakuf. Isn't it true that the road from Gornji Vakuf up to Central Bosnia was actually cut off by the ABiH in January of 1993, and that made travel for all persons, including you, incredibly difficult?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't certain that it was cut off by BiH. We certainly knew that it was very difficult to travel up that road because of unknown entities that were working in that region.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were asked a question in your testimony two years ago, on page 5623 of the Blaskic transcript, whether in approximately January of 1993 the road north from Prozor to Novi Travnik was cut to the HVO, in the sense that it was taken over by the BH army. Your response was, "It was cut in various areas and made travel through there incredibly difficult." That's still your view today, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's still my view, because there was a renegade -- gangs, certainly one known as the Fishhead gang, that were operating on that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that upon your arrival in the area, and before the Busovaca joint commission really got underway, you found in the area of Vitez and Busovaca a state of military, political, and social chaos, essentially?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the whole area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, sir, it was routine to hear complaints on both sides, to be fair, of ethnic cleansing, attacks on remote villages, shootings and snipings, and general harassment of women and children, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, throughout the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed, there were general complaints, and you've alluded to this just a second ago, on the part of both sides, about gangs of thugs roving around the countryside and generally harassing people, blowing up houses and businesses and so forth; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some incidents of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is not just the incidents, but general complaints on both sides about that phenomenon to you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were general complaints to the commission on harassment in villages, harassment of civilians, harassment of women, burning of houses, and aggression towards both Muslims in a Croat village and Croats in Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. When you arrived in the Busovaca area in January of 1993, it's true, is it not, that the HVO had recently lost control of the territory that we have just covered, from Kacuni to Bilalovac, that area, the main supply route had actually been captured by ABiH forces shortly before you arrived; correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that the BiH army had moved into those areas. I actually thought they were Muslim villages which were on those routes and not sort of invaded territory, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that the 333rd Mountain Brigade of the ABiH actually had located its headquarters in the village of Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably had been briefed at some stage, but it didn't have any sort of relevance to me at that stage of numbers, brigades, because there were just so many different ones coming through.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's quite all right, sir. It is a significant number of years ago. Turning to the Busovaca joint commission, I believe that you were sent to Busovaca to sit on this commission, in fact, you were asked to head it up by Brigadier Cumming; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked to head up the military side of the commission, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think that you testified that the commission moved from Busovaca and expanded its focus or the spectrum of activities that it addressed once it moved to Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Actually the name of the commission when it was in Vitez was the Vitez joint commission, and it subsequently became renamed the joint commission after the fighting had broken out in the Lasva Valley in April; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we initially started calling it the Vitez commission but very quickly dropped it to just the joint commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Sayers. I would like to ask the witness whether during the time that he was part of the mixed Vitez commission, whether the scope of that commission's activities -- the scope of work of that committee has changed in the meantime. That is, that the commission had a broader jurisdiction through the change in name, or was it the same scope of jurisdiction that it had been before?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the very first few days, it retained the same scope, but very quickly expanded because of the area we were operating from, we received complaints from both BiH and HVO in and around the Vitez, Zenica, up to Travnik area. So we were asked to include all of that in our scope of operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Major. One minor detail: It's true, is it not, that Mr. Kordic never attended a single meeting of the Busovaca joint commission?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my belief, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Similarly, he never attended any meetings of the Vitez joint commission or participated in any of the negotiations between the various parties throughout the time that you sat on that body; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You made a decision to try to attend about 90 per cent of the meetings of that body, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As many as I could fit in and which were relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that was about 90 per cent of them, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just turn to the second subject that I want to cover with you, the chain of command that you were able to determine with respect to the armed forces of the HVO. There is no doubt in your mind, sir, is there, that all of the HVO forces, including the so-called special purpose units, were under the command and control of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding, that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So, too, were the military jails and detention facilities and the wardens in charge of those facilities, as far as you were aware; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was aware, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And all of the commanders that you encountered within the HVO, uniformly followed the orders of their commanding officer, the commander of the Central Bosnia operative zone; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the one occasion which I outlined, but, yes, the majority of the time they would go under Colonel Blaskic's written or verbal orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This was the conclusion of you as the chief of the intelligence gathering facilities, if you like, of the British forces in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I certainly wasn't chief of intelligence gathering. That wasn't my role when I was with the Busovaca Joint Commission or the joint commission. All I was dealing with were the commission sort of local commanders and the HVO and BiH troops in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. In that capacity, sir, it was apparent to you that the local commanders with whom you dealt with, the one exception that we'll get to in just a second, but it was very apparent to you that the local commanders all respected Colonel Blaskic's authority over them and that you confirmed this in speaking with them; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, sometimes when you visited Bosnian Croat villages and spoke with the local commanders, they occasionally would not or declined to recognise orders issued by the Busovaca Joint Commission; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wouldn't accept orders from the commission unless it had Colonel Blaskic's written letter of authority to do what was being asked of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. In fact, it was clear to you and your colleagues in the United Kingdom armed forces that Colonel Blaskic had a very firm grip on all of the HVO troops that were under his command in the Lasva Valley; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was our understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, sir, it was your view that the local commanders were indeed scared of Colonel Blaskic? They held him in high regard, right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a bit of a fear for him, yes, and held him in quite high regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, you testified, I believe, on page 5.580 of the Blaskic transcript, that: "It was very clear that Colonel Blaskic had full control of all the local commanders and very much controlled those troops in Central Bosnia. Most of the commanders that I met from the HVO were fairly scared of Colonel Blaskic. They would not normally do anything in disagreement to the orders he had given." That's essentially the situation, as you found it, when you were in Central Bosnia, correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, turning to the instance of what you've described, I think, as a little bit of a revolt against this general principle. It's true that you encountered one instance where the Busovaca HVO area commander on his own initiative had ordered a private aid convoy searched because he was actually convinced that it was being used to smuggle arms and ammunition. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were called in, actually, to negotiate for the release of the detained vehicles with the local commander, right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not working with the joint commission at that stage. I was assisting Henk Morsink because he'd asked me to come along with him. But it was the BritBat troops who had been called in to negotiate it. We were just there as escorting and helping.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recall the name of the local commander with whom you dealt, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, it's true, is it not, that this gentleman was clearly under the influence of quite a bit of alcohol?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He'd had a few to drink, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He actually had a lot to drink, hadn't he, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, he had quite a bit to drink, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he was actually extremely angry that the convoy had been allowed through, -- was he not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was very bitter, very angry that the convoy had been allowed to go through and had not been stopped and searched for arms and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So on his own initiative he decided to stop the convoy and search it, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: After two hours of negotiations, that situation was eventually resolved, right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed, sir, you asked this person specifically if he had Colonel Blaskic's authority to do what he did, correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He evaded your question, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made it reasonably clear that he didn't have that authority to do what he had done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Sayers. You are speaking about that individual. The one individual, could you tell us exactly who that is? I'm not really able to follow what person is it you are talking about. Is it the same one who was -- who had drunk too much? Is it the same person? Because I've kind of lost the thread here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm very sorry about that, judge. That's my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just so that we are clear, Mr. Buffini, the local HVO commander who stopped the convoy on his own initiative is the gentleman who was actually clearly under the influence of drink, in your opinion, and angry that the convoy had been allowed through; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same person, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have that person's name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't believe the witness remembers the name. If it was the local commander -- Your Honour, let me just suggest to the witness that it may have been a man by the name of Dusko Grubesic.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't Grubesic. It was somebody else, because I knew Grubesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the suggestion of the name that I just made to you just doesn't jog your memory, I take it, all this time later?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well. Suffice it to say, Mr. Buffini, that you intimated to this gentleman that you were going to make a strong complaint to Colonel Blaskic; did you not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't personally make it. I was with Colonel Duncan and Henk Morsink when we were having the discussion with this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you heard those officers instruct the local HVO commander in no uncertain terms that a strong complaint was going to be made to Colonel Blaskic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Following that, would it be fair to say that the local commander reconsidered his position, albeit reluctantly, and allowed the vehicles that had been detained to be released?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was actually very reluctant to release the vehicles, regardless of whether Colonel Blaskic told him anything or else or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But he nonetheless did so after you had -- after the threat had been made to report him up the chain of command to Colonel Blaskic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was part of the reason why he released it. The other reason was that most of the vehicles had actually been searched and nothing had been found. And we had persuaded him that it was time to let the rest go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning to the final set of questions that I wanted to ask you. This concerns your sighting of HV troops in the area of Prozor. Did I understand you to say that the sum total of instances of sightings of HV troops that you were made aware of throughout your tour from January to July was two?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally sighted on two occasions, but there were more incidents that I was involved in from the watchkeeping duties where reports came back that HV troops were using route triangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, did you actually speak to any of the soldiers within these coaches yourself?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't speak to anyone at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you speak Croatian at all?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you use any interpreters to try to pose questions to any of the soldiers that were in these coaches?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had no interpreters with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. So it would be fair to say that you don't know what the mission of the soldiers was, correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You don't know who that commander was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And your conclusions regarding their providence was based upon, first, HV patches on their uniforms and, second, on Croatian licence plates, I think you said, that you saw on the buses themselves?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How did you know that they were Croatian licence plates, specifically?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having spent quite a bit of my time in and around Split and in Croatia, I recognised Croatian licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that a Croatian licence plate has a chequerboard symbol plus five little symbols on the top of it denoting the five regions in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall specifically, but I certainly knew at the time what was -- what was what.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever see any licence plates of vehicles that were operating in the territory of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw vehicles in and around sort of Vitez, if that's what you mean, and other areas, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know what the difference between a Croatian licence plate is and a Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna licence plate is?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did at the time, but I can't exactly recall at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You also related an incident in which these troops had, in your opinion, been fighting. You don't know precisely where they had been fighting, though, do you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you don't know under whose command they had been fighting, do you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You never received any information whatsoever that any of these HV troops had moved up the main supply route from Herzegovina into Central Bosnia, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up -- sorry? Your definition of Central Bosnia and Herzegovina locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir. You never received any information that any HV troops of the type that you sighted had moved from the Prozor area up to the Lasva Valley, for example, or to the Kiseljak area, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no information specifically on that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you never saw any such troops in the central Lasva Valley or Central Bosnia, Kiseljak, Vitez, Busovaca area yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, indeed, you are of the opinion that wherever those troops had been fighting, they had not been involved in combat activities in Central Bosnia itself, in the Vitez, Busovaca, Novi Travnik, Kiseljak area; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in those areas, but in and around the Prozor area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you have no specific personal knowledge that either Colonel Blaskic or the HVO was paid or financed by the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And no personal knowledge that the activities of any of the officers in Central Bosnia were directed, coordinated or supervised by responsible military or political officials within the Republic of Croatia, correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No direct knowledge of it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Similarly, have you no personal knowledge that the Republic of Croatia ever issued specific instructions concerning the commission of actions by Colonel Blaskic or by the HVO in Central Bosnia, have you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw any instructions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You have no specific knowledge that the Republic of Croatia entrusted Colonel Blaskic with the specific task of performing lawful actions on its behalf, but that he, in discharging that task, breached some sort of obligation owed by the Republic of Croatia; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that -- of those actions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Certainly, it would be fair to say that you never saw Colonel Blaskic or any other soldier in Central Bosnia dressed in the uniform of the forces of the Republic of Croatia; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw Colonel Blaskic dressed in uniform, but obviously there were other HV soldiers that I saw in the Prozor area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. But I am talking about the --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the Vitez, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. And it's true, is it not, that the general staff of the HVO was headquartered in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you yourself had some dealings, I believe, with the chief of the general staff, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Brigadier Petkovic reported to the President of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna and to the Department of Defence of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. And not to anybody in Croatia, as far as you are aware?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was aware, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The final series of questions that I've got for you, sir, concern the ceasefire negotiations that occurred, I believe April the 20th, 21st of 1993 involving Brigadier Petkovic and General Halilovic. It's true, is it not, that in none of those negotiations -- let me rephrase the question. Mr. Kordic wasn't involved in any of those negotiations, as far as you are aware, was he?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I was aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And after the ceasefire agreement had been concluded, you took the senior military commanders of both sides on a personal tour of the front lines in Vitez, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I escorted them, but wasn't personally taking them around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You've testified that Brigadier Petkovic was the chief of the general staff of the HVO. It's true that his counterpart, the commanding officer of the ABiH forces, if you like, was General Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were present in person as General Halilovic and Brigadier Petkovic were giving orders to their troops on the ground, right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Incidently, in the high level negotiations that preceded the signature of the ceasefire agreement on April the 21st, I believe it was, 1993, as far as you are aware, the issue of the fighting in Ahmici and the consequences of that fighting were never actually raised or discussed between the negotiators, were they?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe they were. I can't recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Buffini. My name is Bozidar Kovacic. I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Cerkez, together with my colleague, Mr. Mikulicic. At one point in time you mentioned that you were passing by Sinj and you saw training grounds for soldiers. Sinj is in Croatia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training camp was on the route to Sinj, but not actually in Sinj. But it was in Croatia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At that time Croatia was under the aggression of the Yugoslav People's Army that was under Serbia's control; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: While you were in Divulje, essentially Croatia was at a state of war, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it strange, then, in any way to see a concentration of military forces, including a training camp?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't strange at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to put a few questions to you. It seems to me that it is not clear after your testimony, and after Mr. Morsink's testimony some details remained unclear, so I would like to seek your assistance on those matters. Yesterday it seemed, on the basis of what you said, as if the Busovaca commission was moved to Nova Bila; that is to say, to the ECMM offices next to the British Battalion already in March 1993. I'd like to put the following to you: Mr. Morsink said here -- as for the transcript, this is page 121 on the 71st day -- in response to the Prosecutor's question whether the first meeting was held on the 8th of May, that is to say, of the local commission in Busovaca, and whether that was the first meeting in Vitez. Morsink said, and I quote, "Then we saw a video and the pictures of the persons present." Do you agree on this, that the first meeting of the commission at the new premises near the British camp was only on the 8th of May?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the first meeting of the joint command, which was the BiH and HVO armies, was in May. The Busovaca commission was in March. And it moved to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So, in your opinion, when did it have its first meeting in Vitez, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first meeting of the Vitez commission was middle of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I would like to present Exhibit Z548,1. Could the usher please show it to the witness. Could the Registrar help me on this. This was tendered during the first part of your testimony. You saw this document. This is the ECMM report from the 17th of March. I would like to draw your attention to the last page in this report. Please look at the penultimate paragraph. Point 7. It says "Proposal" in capital letters. It says here that the commission -- well, I mean, this could have been the 17th of March that the commission -- well, first of all, it's called a proposal, so I'm not sure whether it was a decision or not. Secondly, it says here that the commission would move to Vitez when the office premises, the building next door to the British headquarters -- that's what it says in brackets -- together with all the necessary equipment, will actually be able to be used, and it says explicitly not before that. So it is only on the 17th of March that this decision was passed. I imagine that under those circumstances, the building that was used later for meetings could not have been arranged in such a short period of time. On the basis of this, it seems obvious that the commission could not have held its meeting in Vitez as early as you had said. Does this perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think it's time for a question. The question is, does that make you change your mind about the date, Mr. Buffini?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of this proposal was the 17th of March. Within one week we were in the Vitez house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So we can agree that you were in that office in Vitez somewhere toward the end of March, around the 25th, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, towards the end of March we were in the Vitez house, I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And on the 4th of April, you went on leave?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, before you went on leave, you did not meet Mario Cerkez, ever; right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I'd met him prior, personally, at that stage, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Actually, can one say that the events in Vitez until the point when you went on leave were not in the focus of your attention? I'm referring to the ECMM and UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was very little happening in and around Vitez itself at that stage, so that was not our focus, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us a lot about the work of the commission, and you mentioned Cerkez's presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the registry for their assistance. Let us show the witness the photographs from the meeting -- actually I'm talking about Exhibits Z2531 and Z2529. Perhaps you can use the copies I have so that we could move on more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: These are photographs that we got from the video that was shown during Mr. Morsink's testimony. We see a person here with a badge. Can you recognise this person? A patch, rather.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the patch, and I believe the person is Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the other picture now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is this Mr. Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you recognise him here today in this courtroom, do you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, as for the meetings in Bila, in the time period when you were there, after the 25th, Mr. Cerkez came to these meetings only twice; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was either two or three times. It wasn't more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I remind you of the following: In addition to that, you met him and talked to him at least on one more occasion, and this was in front of Cerkez's headquarters in Vitez, and probably one more time, with the participation of other persons in Vitez, but you do not know exactly when; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, is it correct that you never came to Cerkez's office?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went into his office, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The members of the commission, when it moved, and also before that, when it moved to Vitez, were Mr. Nakic on behalf of the HVO, you said, and actually the level of the representatives of the parties to the conflict was Nakic as the representative of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia and Merdan as the representative of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So in principle, that was the level at which discussions were held and at which agreements were reached when possible; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the levels that we asked for cooperation and clarification of certain orders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that from time to time, for practical reasons, lower commanders were also invited to attend commission meetings, even down to the level of commanders in villages, in individual villages?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We normally had at least three representatives from local villages and other commands to address the complaints and the problems that we were dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I conclude, generally speaking, that when these lower-level commanders attended, they were not negotiators; they were there for practical reasons, in order to obtain information and to convey information, or to go for an on-site inspection? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there to facilitate our work when we had to move into those areas, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said to us that Mr. Nakic, the representative of the HVO, did not really have a great deal of authority. Did you know that Nakic's formal position in the Operative Zone was chief of staff in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, so the second person in line in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'd been informed that he was the deputy commander of the Operative Zone in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I believe that we will agree that regardless of whether he was formally chief of staff or deputy commander or assistant commander, he was the second man in line, basically; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was our understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It was obvious that this second man in command in the HVO, regardless of what his exact title was, did not have a great deal of authority, at least not judging by Nakic's example?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When Cerkez attended meetings, and you mentioned them, he acted as a local commander, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the local commander for the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On occasions when he was supposed to say something related to the positions that were under the control of his troops, he did that, and it was obvious that he was independent and responsible for his troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was clear to us that he had command and authority over his troops in his area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us be quite clear on this. You never said until now, but I imagine it is undeniable, you know that he was the commander of the Vitez Brigade, the Viteska Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You know that this was a Home Guards brigade with its seat in Vitez, its headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of your definition of "Home Guard," but it was certainly an operational military unit in the Vitez area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You don't have any specific knowledge about the concrete zones of responsibility of that brigade, do you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, moving on ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for 20 minutes -- yes, Mr. Nice, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was informed that you probably wanted to know what our position was in relation to depositions for later witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next witness, who has come at short notice to make sure that we didn't waste time this week, would be ready to start this morning, although things might be a little scruffier than they would be if we hadn't had him for such a short period of time. I think if we were to start him either this morning or tomorrow morning, we would probably have pretty well a full week with no wasted time, so of course we are anxious to proceed by deposition if that's appropriate. My only concern about the next witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: About the witness after?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, no, the witness coming this morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me interrupt to say this, that we are in a position to sit this afternoon, so there will be an extra hour and a half available.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's very helpful. My only concern about today's witness, then, is that he would be giving really quite detailed -- or capable of giving quite detailed evidence in relation to maps and about locations in and around Busovaca, and we don't yet know whether the Chamber is going to be able to make any site visit. Absent such a visit, such evidence may be the more difficult for a judge to take second-hand, without having the witness in front of him, and the maps. That's our only concern. For our part, obviously, we would like to get on, but we don't want to commit the Chamber to having evidence in a less satisfactory way when the evidence is quite important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I understand that, but I think it's not too difficult for somebody to pick the matter up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Particularly if it's possible to have a video of all the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As there will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So we will make an application in the half-hour break, a written application for deposition evidence for the remaining two witnesses this week. I don't know how long Mr. Kovacic is going to be with Mr. Buffini, but in any event, we can start on the other witness sometime today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. 20 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, do you know the date on which that unfortunate incident in Ahmici took place?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, because it was during the time I was back in the United Kingdom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we heard from you that you know of an explanation which Cerkez gave on why these troops were in Ahmici. Did you hear this from Cerkez or you heard him say this somewhere, or did you read about it on a report?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. What statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you heard that Cerkez had given a statement regarding Ahmici, in the sense that the Muslims had attacked Ahmici. My question is did he give this statement to you, did you hear it from third persons, or did you read about it in a report?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd actually heard it in one of the meetings we were in, but I cannot definitely say it was directly from Mr. Cerkez, person to person, but the quote was as attributed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In this context did you, perhaps, ever hear of Cerkez discussing and being asked about Ahmici by Payam Akhavan, an U.N. investigator, and that on this occasion Colonel Bob Stewart was also present?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recollect that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, from your monitoring the situation, did you learn that in Novi Travnik there was a large-sized HOS unit which was operating in conjunction with the HVO? Did you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have knowledge of Novi Travnik. I was aware, when I first arrived in Busovaca in January, that HOS units were operating, but I wasn't sure where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that they predominantly had black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in the early stages, before the escalation of the conflict, there were both Croats and Muslims within their units?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll not pursue that. In the meetings of the commission, topics ranged from attempts to negotiate to maintaining ceasefire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is there any reason, apart from mutual accusations, to reopen the Ahmici incident which had taken -- the incident which had taken place several weeks earlier?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was always our point at meetings to try and find out what had happened and who had perpetrated Ahmici, but before we could come onto that central issue there were other smaller issues which had to be decided first before anything serious could be addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move onto another topic. You told us when you spoke with Cerkez, and that was obviously the conversation in front of this cinema theatre where you and Mr. Morsink were there, and he told you about the house torched in Kruscica, he complained. And you went with another representative to take a look at them. First of all, do you agree that this representative of Cerkez was Boro Jozic? Does that name ring any bells for you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That certainly sounds familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the person who we saw in the videotape. Thank you. Second, in order for you to come to arrive in Kruscica from Vitez, you needed to cross a line of separation just before entering Kruscica. Do you remember crossing that line when you arrived at a location where you did not find any burned houses?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to take a circuitous route because we couldn't travel directly to the location because there were mines on the road. So we had to travel to another route to get to Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In other words, as far as the location is concerned, we are certain that you arrived on the side in Kruscica which was under the BiH Army control; was that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We visited houses both in the BiH Army controlled area and also the HVO controlled area en route to and from Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I believe that I made a mistake. I didn't ask you properly. You went to search for a location where, according to Cerkez's complaint, some houses had been burnt down. My question is: Are you sure that where you went to look and didn't find those houses, you found yourself in the territory controlled by the other side, the other army?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were absolutely certain we had the right location because we asked Mr. Cerkez's representative for the exact location, and that's where we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, the Cerkez representative, that is Jozic, at the very end of the excerpt which -- that we saw, he expressly states that there was another location where those houses could be. In other words, that there was another location where you were supposed to look.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And we went there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you didn't find anything?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: A couple of points. One is Kruscica, and I believe that you had a fairly good understanding of the situation. Kruscica is a fairly large village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a reasonable sized village, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see whether Krusica had completely separate parts? It is on a hill -- in the hills and then there is -- on the slope there is another built-up area and then there is an additional one on the other side?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I seem to recollect that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for a possibility that you could not have observed all points in the area called Kruscica in order to confirm whether this allegation was true or not, that, objectively speaking, you were not in a position to do so?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in a full position to go where we needed to go to identify the Croat houses which had been -- which we had been told were on fire. We could not find any houses in the Kruscica area or in the area between Vitez and Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As regards this situation which was ongoing at the time, that was in early May, militarily speaking it was a pretty chaotic situation, given the distribution of forces. On the basis of your knowledge of the HVO at the time in that particular locale, do you believe that the brigade commander, specifically Mario Cerkez, had accurate and correct information, or that, given the circumstances, it is reasonable to believe that there was information that was not accurate and up to date?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the information was relayed by hand-held radios which all of the HVO commanders had that we met, and I believe that the information was known to Mr. Cerkez on all the units under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In respect of this topic, just one additional question. Did you ever know of any other occasions when a commander had wrong or bad information?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were incidences in very small, isolated villages where some information wasn't getting back. But on the whole, front lines, no, the information was definitely available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Moving on to the trench digging, first, just to clarify one small point, yesterday you said that the representative of the Red Cross, Madam Claire Podbielski, complained to Nakic and Cerkez in the sense that she was learning about situations where prisoners had been used to dig trenches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This morning, you confirmed that you had previously given a statement to the OTP representatives, and in this statement, you expressly stated -- and let me read it to you, and perhaps you can clarify what the difference was. You said [in English]: "Two or three meetings of the joint commission were also attended by a representative of the ICRC, Claire Podbielski, and her relief, whose name I cannot recall. At those meetings, Claire told Nakic and possibly Cerkez." [Interpreted] If you had given this statement in 1997 -- that is, more than two years ago -- can you today confirm that Madam Claire Podbielski complained to Cerkez, or is it possible that it was perhaps also to Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meetings, it was probably -- and I say that with hindsight -- to Cerkez, but she definitely addressed him, on an occasion I saw, with that accusation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is, if Cerkez did attend that meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two separate instances. With the meetings, when she came in, I believe Mr. Cerkez was there; and on the occasion when Mr. Morsink and I had asked about the burning houses and the trench digging, Ms. Podbielski was also there and addressed Mr. Cerkez at that time about prisoners and trench digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you recall that she was present at the conversation with Cerkez outside of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of one of the meetings, yes, but I believe also in one of the meetings as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you recall, was that that conversation which you had with Cerkez in front of the cinema theatre? That is, his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the conversation, and we were videoed by the ITN news crew at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Then you said that, in fact, with respect to this accusation about trench digging, the most you saw was actually freshly dug trenches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all we saw, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps describe this location for us, the location where you saw this?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location was between Stari Vitez and Vitez, on the HVO side of Vitez, facing Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, may I perhaps remind you, you saw with your own eyes that the town of Vitez, the Old Vitez, Stari Vitez and Vitez, the urban area, was divided. The army did not need any trenches on that location. They didn't have trenches there at any time during the conflict. I put it to you that you saw these trenches somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trenches we saw were around the area of conflict between Stari Vitez and Vitez, and it was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You cannot say where it is between Stari Vitez and the town of Vitez, or between Stari Vitez and the other direction, towards the church, the Catholic Church?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically recollecting churches, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So all you recall is that it was somewhere in that area, but you cannot say specifically exactly where, very well. Can you tell us you agree that at no time did you see members of the Vitez Brigade using prisoners for trench digging?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw no incidents of them using prisoners trench digging, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
