utterances.text: Thank you. A couple of questions on another topic. You told us about two decomposing bodies which the BH army soldiers had buried just a couple of hours before you arrived, and then it was shown to you on the video. You know what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you again were present with Mr. Morsink?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same day as we met Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Unless I missed it, yesterday you said -- I don't think that yesterday you said what location that was at.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mentioned no location because it didn't ring a bell. I couldn't recall the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I can refresh your recollection, you said to the investigators that that was in Zaselje, but in the tape we saw, that could not have been Zaselje because there was forest there, and the tape which was shown to you showed a location where there were houses. So couldn't it perhaps have been Kruscica instead?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was definitely not Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you cannot say for sure that it was Zaselje?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't identify the town specifically, but it was definitely not Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But it was definitely somewhere in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can I perhaps put it to you -- I mean, can you, in fact, say where -- was it closer to Vitez, closer to Busovaca, closer to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a map, looking at a map, it was probably three or four kilometres south of Kruscica, somewhere in that area, but very, very small tracks leading up to it, which maps I have seen don't show that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And as far as regards Zaselje which we mentioned here, did you perhaps know that this was actually a Serb village, that there were no Muslims there? Did you have an opportunity to find this out? There were no Croat Muslim hostilities there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware it was a Serb village, just that that was the location we were told to go to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll let that alone regarding location. You said that the local commander, the Muslim local commander, you said because of a terrible stench they had buried the bodies a couple of hours before you had arrived. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then you were told that again a Muslim journalist had filmed these bodies before they were buried, that he videotaped, made a videotape of that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And it was said that there was no dispute that for 22 days those bodies were lying on no-man's land?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had been informed that they had been out in the open in no-man's land for about 22 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that they could not have been removed because they were in a minefield?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was a minefield or just an area where there was still fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then you viewed this tape; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I viewed the short tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then you viewed this tape through the camera viewfinder; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, that screen, and forgive my technical education, that screen where you can view this image is some three by three centimetres big; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite small, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, maybe I am hurrying you to a conclusion. But you have no forensic education based on your previous experience?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no forensic experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did, perhaps, Mr. Morsink say anything about him having any such forensic experience?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And there was no one else with a similar experience of that kind who was around?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no forensic experts around at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The person who drew this expert conclusion was Mr. Morsink?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We both concluded from our sightings that things had happened to those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The conclusion about the cause of death?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the cause of death. The fact that the bodies had been mutilated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. What was the cause of the mutilation? And we are talking the summer, this was in the middle of the summer, so the cause of this mutilation may have been a mine which -- on which they may have stepped?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The marks on their necks was definitely of something of a wire or a knife. It was a straight line mark. And on the wrists it was evident that it was a straight line and not a mine or a bomb, which I have seen bodies and pictures of those damages to people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On an image which was a size of three by three?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The video camera went quite close up on the areas that I discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the location in which the corpses were found was on the edge of a forest? This was a densely forested area, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of the location where the bodies were found. All I knew is that they had been brought back to their village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you conclude on the basis of any insignia in the image that these were members of either Croatian or Bosniak Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The areas of the body we saw had camouflage clothing, but no insignias were seen anywhere at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, you cannot exclude that the Muslim commander who had produced the tape had given you information which he wanted because you only got his side of the story?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got several sides from the BiH Army, plus one of the bodies recovered was the son of one of the people in that village, and he was very upset about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you don't know in which -- in whose zone of responsibility it was, or did you know whose zone of responsibility it was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did at the time, but today I couldn't say the exact location where it was coming from. It was in and around the Vitez area. That's as far as I can go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And let's move on. You told us that representatives of the ABiH, that in the meetings in which they were present with Cerkez, they obviously projected a hatred against Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, can you perhaps recall whether this was a general attitude of everyone sitting on the ABiH side or was it the attitude or the position of only one of them?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very specifically the attitude of one, but the feeling was that for most of the others as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may ask the usher to please place this picture on the ELMO again. Mr. Buffini, do you recall that in several meetings one of the members of the ABiH team was Mr. Klestura, a very sort of a strong built, dark looking man, a dinara type. He is wearing a hat. Can you see him in that picture? Was that the man who really hated Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Out of the three persons in the picture, you cannot identify him as any of them?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very much so, yes. This man here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So the one in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But that is Sefkija Djidic. You knew Sefkija, correct? You had contact with him, as you did with other representatives of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Buffini, did you ever hear of Sefkija Djidic and Cerkez having worked together for 12 or 15 years and that they were very close friends, as a matter of fact? Are you quite sure that it was Sefkija who projected this hatred?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In your previous statement made to the investigators, you never mentioned this hatred, did you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I mentioned the fact that in some meetings the BiH commanders, when they came in, and Mr. Cerkez was there, were rather angry, they were upset, and they felt very uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. You also said to us that Cerkez on several occasions flatly rejected the accusations levelled at his units, that they would jeopardise the ceasefire. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Buffini, will we agree that Cerkez always mentioned in these words or others the very same argument, the very same response, so-to-speak, "It is not my units. It is not units under my command. It is units that are beyond control. Bandits, hooligans, whatever." But did he consistently say that, "They were not my units." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He often gave that as an excuse, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, you are a professional soldier. Please tell me, a commander is responsible only for troops that are under his command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If somebody else does something, if somebody else breaks the ceasefire, that is to say a person who is not a member of Cerkez's unit, should Cerkez be held responsible for the fact that he broke the ceasefire too?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the person is not under the command and is not part of that unit, then Mr. Cerkez has no authority over him and should not take the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be natural, then, that when a commander is faced with such accusations, "This is not my unit and I do not wish to discuss it," from a military point of view isn't that a relevant answer?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an answer which is a good excuse for the fact that the troops operating in that area should be under his command. So if it's happening in that area, then he should have been advised or given indication that these troops were in his area of operation, and therefore coming under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, yesterday and today we ascertained beyond a reasonable doubt that there were other units as well. For example, yesterday we heard the story about the unit that was moving around throughout the valley in Golf vehicles. Is Cerkez responsible for that kind of a unit too?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that unit is operating under the guise of the HVO forces, then if they are operating in his unit and he's given command of them, then, yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Kovacic. I would like to ask the witness -- he's just said some words about the various chains of command. In your opinion, Major Buffini, could Mr. Cerkez be considered as having had a territorial area under his responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he would have a very definite area that he was responsible for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell the Chamber what, in your opinion, that territorial area of responsibility was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, sir, but it was definitely an area around Vitez, the town of Vitez, and some of the outlying areas close to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We asked the witness earlier on whether he knew that, and he said that he didn't, and he repeated the same answer once again now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: However, you touched upon another subject a few minutes ago. You said if other units were subordinated to him; actually, you cannot claim on any basis that any other unit was subordinated to Cerkez in the Lasva River Valley area, with the exception of the Vitez Brigade. Is there any other knowledge you would like to share with us on that note?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, I'm going to stop this. This is argument which you are engaging in with the witness. You are not asking him to give evidence. He has stated what he has known. His answer in relation to the other questions was, as I understood it, hypothetical. I shall, in order to clarify the position, ask the question, but I'm not going to allow more argument on this very point. Mr. Buffini, just to make it plain, did you know of any other units under the command of Mr. Cerkez in the Lasva Valley at the relevant time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I was not aware of any other units that were under his command. We had no such information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And I understood you to be giving a hypothetical answer about units being under the command of a particular commander.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If other troops are moved into an area, a specific task force, or special forces, or engineers of some kind, normally they would be given a commander who they would report to in that area, so they would be either under control or under command of that area commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. So the answer is that the witness knows of no other units under the command of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, for going too far, perhaps, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need for apologies. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just a small question related to your visit to the cinema, where there were persons who had been detained, when the important generals came in and when they said to these persons that they would be free. There is no doubt, on the basis of what you have said, that all those persons were military able persons, military able men; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that all men between the ages of 18 and 55 were considered military men. So yes, all of them in that building were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you also said that the vast majority claimed that they would not feel safe if they were to get out without UNPROFOR protection?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That was their feeling, that objectively speaking it was dangerous outside, and that is why they did not want to leave without protection?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They felt they would be shot or harassed in moving back to their own home locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just in passing, Mr. Buffini, those days when you came to the centre of Vitez, and you did go to the centre of Vitez, did you notice that there were traces of any shelling on the main buildings in the centre of Vitez, like the post office, the medical centre, all these other buildings around the cinema? Did you notice any traces of that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the buildings in the whole Vitez area had some form of damage from shrapnel, direct gunfire, that type of incident, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Finally, I just want to be sure about this. On the ground in Vitez, in the immediate vicinity of Vitez, you spent a total amount of two months there as you worked for the commission. Let us confirm the dates. You came to Busovaca on the 6th of March, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On and around that date, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You went on leave on the 4th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is to say about a month, you worked there for about a month, and then you returned from leave on the 25th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually think it was a bit earlier when I came back up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The 25th is mentioned in your previous statement, and that's what you said yesterday, I believe. But all right, we agree on that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably two or three days -- round about that time frame, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you left the area, as you said in your statement, towards the end of May, so that is --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't specifically leave the area. I left my duties with the joint commission towards the end of May. I stayed in the Vitez area probably for another two, three weeks, until early June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Correct. But you were involved with the commission until the end of May, towards the end of May; right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is the only period during which you dealt in this subject matter, that is to say, the Muslim/Croat conflict in Vitez and its surroundings; after that, you were involved in other matters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was involved in other matters but obviously had a close link with Henk Morsink, who was still involved with matters in the Vitez area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Buffini. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: A few points. I'd like to just address, before I start redirect, a point that arose during cross-examination. A question was posed to the witness by counsel, and to the best of my quotational abilities, you have no specific knowledge that the Republic of Croatia entrusted Colonel Blaskic with the specific task of performing lawful actions on his behalf, but that he, in discharging those tasks or that task, either breached or reached, depending on the transcript, some sort of obligation. It is unclear, and in a sense hampers our understanding of what we can ask on redirect as to this point, what possible lawful actions might have been referred to. Perhaps the witness would benefit by having some inclination; we certainly would. I think it was inappropriate for us to object at the time, but I am concerned that there was no explanation to the witness of what type of lawful action the Republic of Croatia could possibly have that would be fulfilled by Colonel Blaskic on the territory of BiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't imagine the witness can help us very much about that, if at all. It's not a very clear question, I quite agree, and it's probably something which should have been dealt with at the time. Perhaps counsel could note what's been said, and in due course, enlighten us as to what he means. Can you help anything about that, Mr. Buffini?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: However, it was raised that the Republic of Croatia was engaged in conflict during this time, and would you have been aware of -- or would you think it within the normal course of military prudence to assign military resources to another sovereign state, if in fact that state from which the resources were coming was engaged in some conflict?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would certainly be good reasons for it, if they could prevent their state being attacked in other locations by supporting and offering assistance in other places.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In other words, a political -- sorry, let me give the interpreters a chance. A political or military objective or purpose would have to be served for the Republic of Croatia to engage in such activity?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very much so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I object to the leading nature of that question, Your Honour. This is redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The fact that Mr. Kordic was not present, to your recollection, at any of the joint commission meetings, did that indicate to you that -- or are you familiar with any other political representatives or any other representatives of the political parties early on in the commission days, from the SDA or from the HDZ party, being present?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, I don't think they were present in either the Busovaca or the Vitez meetings, but I was certainly aware of their presence when I attended a meeting in Zenica at the hotel there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was Mate Boban ever present at any of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The fact that Colonel Blaskic may have had defined command and control powers in his Operative Zone, does that in your mind mean that there is no other authority who could override an order of Colonel Blaskic or who could influence his orders?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a military perspective, I don't believe that anybody under his command or working under his rank of responsibility could counteract any of his authority, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: An individual, however, operating in territories of the former Yugoslavia -- excuse me, let me rephrase that. There could be an individual who would fulfil the role of political officer? Are you familiar with such role?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very familiar with political officers, and we suspected that there must be some element of political input because of the pure nature of the Yugoslavian military, having had such close links and working on Soviet-style lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Had you been made aware expressly that when Mario Cerkez came to these meetings, that he had previously been an acting commander of the Viteska Brigade and had been a deputy commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade? Did you know of his extensive HVO command experience?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't specifically know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You described the discipline that Colonel Blaskic imposed in his Operative Zone as one that caused fear by soldiers. Did anyone take to task the soldier who refused, albeit in perhaps a questionably sober state, to honour the order of Colonel Blaskic? Or in the alternative, did you find it strange that someone under such a strict chain of command could get away with that and be left in that position in an obviously well-known convoy?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we found it very strange that somebody would contravene orders which had clearly been given that the convoy could pass through, and very strange that he actually stayed in the position he was in after that incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just to confirm, the HV soldiers who were described as battle weary, were they viewed by you solidly within the territory of the sovereign state of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL BUFFINI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were literally one kilometre north of Prozor, and I viewed them personally with my driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Nothing further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Buffini, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it, and you are released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I start the next witness this afternoon and use the other seven minutes this morning to start dealing with one of the administrative matters that is outstanding?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We have to adjourn promptly at 1.00, I should say, and we won't be sitting again until 2.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we deal with the administrative matter in private session, for good reason?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before I deal with the next witness, a small point to tidy up. I distributed a couple of weeks ago two maps, showing front lines, with various markings on them. Lest I overlook the point, I am informed that there is an error on each map; it's a simple error to correct. In each case, the legend or chart showing to what various shapes relate should be taken as correct, but where particular units are marked, there are two errors. That which is marked "16" should be marked "17," and that which is marked "17" should be marked "18," and then the units will correctly tie up with the legend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness Jennings produced a useful map last week, the JNA map that he said was provided to him by the defendant Kordic. We had a part of it copied in colour and a part of it copied in black and white, but the full map in colour has now been reproduced, and to make sense, should be given not the exhibit number that's been put on it in bold but the Exhibit Number 2781,2, and I think that is now available for distribution. All right. Apparently it's been corrected already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And has it been distributed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It may be useful in relation to this witness's evidence, although I think an even better map may serve us well on this occasion. But nevertheless, that JNA map is available. I turn to this witness, in respect of whom an application for protection by way of face distortion and pseudonym is sought. His summary shows his proximity to one of the defendants and his ability to identify by name wrongdoers at a nasty level, and his evidence is of course, arguably, of considerable importance as against one of the defendants. He lost between 11 and 16 members of his immediate family in the conflict, I am informed. He is a person who will have, in due course, to return to Busovaca, I think by reason of the rehousing programme that obliges people in certain circumstances to be returned to their original homes. In his judgement, the people doing things in the war are still in power in the same locality. His job involves driving through areas of different ethnicity in any event, and he has concerns for his safety if his full identity is known. He has proved otherwise entirely cooperative and helpful in providing as much detail as is apparently available to him through his memory, and we would ask that he be granted protection limited to facial distortion and the use of a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Kordic is not opposed to these suggestions, but we would like to have the open session as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The Cerkez Defence does not have any objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, this is to be in open session, but with the distortion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll make the order, the pseudonym being --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym of the witness is Witness T.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before the witness is brought in, if the usher could just help me for one second, there's a map that will be of use to the Tribunal, and it's sometimes helpful if preparation is done before the witness comes and fumbles with things on the ELMO. This map may be distributed as 2271, and if I can have a copy of it, or I can provide this one and have another one back for me. The area we need lay on the ELMO is -- and we can probably go in closer than that, if the technical booth would like to move in closer onto Busovaca. I guess that's probably about far enough. That's fine. The witness will produce his own maps, hand-drawn. They are two sheets that join together. The Chamber can see the road running initially south-southwest and then effectively south from -- no, it can't. To the right of the last "A" of Busovaca, there's a road running -- a white road running south. Further east of that, there's a coloured road running south-southwest and then bearing south. And the witness's drawing, as I understand it, is of that road or track, although by the way he has drawn it, it would appear to travel in an entirely different direction. But it may be helpful if I indicate that that is the road leading down to Kupres, and possibly further, that he will have drawn for us. And it may be possible to speed things up by laying his map on top of the formal map and removing his map as and when necessary. Thank you very much. There are little clips of exhibits that can possibly be distributed to the Judges now, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you would like to sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: For the purposes of giving evidence, you will be known as Witness T. I'm going to ask you first a few questions about your history.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, because some of them may reveal matters of identity, may we have, just for a couple of minutes, a private session to deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 and 4. In the spring of 1991, when the HDZ started, did you see anything of Kordic, and was there any conversation about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic. Yes. I'm sorry, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour, but the spring of '91 was mentioned. This is outside of the scope of the indictment, so I don't see the relevance of that question. The indictment starts with the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Counsel may lay the foundation for his questions and deal with relevant matters of background. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness T, was there a conversation with the defendant Kordic about his having been a Communist? If so, tell us just in a sentence what was said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I talked in 1991, I believe that was in November, so I talked to him on the occasion when the HDZ and the SDA had an electoral win in Busovaca; that is, when they jointly won the elections and came into power. We ran into each other on the street on the way between the bus station and the intersection of my and his streets. On the way there we made jokes, jokes about the Communist having lost power in Busovaca. Among other things, the topic of the authority was raised, that is, whether the Communist government was going to prove to have been better or the Muslim Croat, or that is the SDA/HDZ coalition. At that time on that occasion he said that this new government was certainly going to be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness T, I should have asked you to look at this piece of paper that the usher will bring you, simply to confirm by the answer "yes" if it be the case that that is your proper name that's being shown to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraphs 5 to 7 I'll deal with summarily. Did Mate Boban take over as President of the entire HDZ, whilst Cicak, Zvonimir Cicak, the local President, a person who was not, in your judgement, an extremist, was he replaced by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are not going to get on with constant interruption. Your last interruption, Mr. Naumovski, had no point. Now, what is it this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies for standing up, but I believe that this witness was no member of HDZ, and there are questions asked about the HDZ without any foundations having been laid for it. My apologies again for raising this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, is it disputed that Mr. Boban was the President of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is in question is the date when he became the President of the HDZ, because Mr. Boban was not the President of the HDZ throughout this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As for Mr. Cicak, we've heard evidence about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, and he was not the President of the HDZ, as is stated here. This is the ground for my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Insofar as it's relevant, the witness can say what he understood, but there is other evidence about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think I am just going to move on to save time, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 9. Witness T, we are going to pass over your knowledge of local politics. But just to paint the picture, is Busovaca a big or a little town, and just "yes" or "no," did you as a local resident come to know who the local political party leaders were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Busovaca is a small town. It is a developing town. I had an opportunity to walk about in this town, this small town, and I came to meet most of the people there. And I knew a majority of the local leaders there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was your experience of and judgement of the position and power of Kordic in the municipality once he became President of the local HDZ or once he became President of the HDZ for Central Bosnia? What was your experience of and impression of his power and authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At that time he had a political authority in the territory of Busovaca municipality, and not only in Busovaca municipality, but that would include Vitez, Novi Travnik, Fojnica, Kiseljak, Stari Travnik and Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Apart from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: After the state of war was declared in Busovaca, all the civilian power structures were mobilised and turned into military ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 11. Before the existence of the HVO, is it right that the Croats and Muslims were participating together in Territorial Defence fighting the Serbs, and were you a member of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 10. At the time of the formation of the HDZ, were you aware of Kordic's position in the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He had a duty of the deputy vice-president of the War Presidency of the local government.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 13. I want some short assistance with certain formations and with what uniforms or markings they displayed. The ZNG, Peoples Guard Unit, what uniforms did they wear? Did they show their markings in any other way, their identity in any other way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The ZNG was established in 1991. Its original purpose was to provide military security of the religious places of worship of the Croatian people. They wore camouflage uniforms with insignia "ZNG."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: HOS, what about their uniforms and any insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The HOS members wore black uniforms with insignia stating "HOS."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At that time did the defendant Kordic have headquarters somewhere in Busovaca? If so, where? And using the pointer that the usher will provide you and using the map on the right, but not moving your head, you can point out very approximately where it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At that time, while the ZNG and HOS troops were still in existence, the headquarters was not in the urban area itself. Later on, that is in 1992, there were -- there was more of a -- there were more units, such as special police units, then intervention platoons and MUP, which had mobilised Croats, were all in the -- were all gathered in this area and their headquarters was in the Hotel Tisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you point to the Hotel Tisa? Was it on the main road running through Busovaca? If so, just give us an idea where it was, familiarising yourself with the map again. And you have to point, I'm afraid, to the map on the overhead projector, and you'll see that your pointing will then become visible on the television screen. Now, you're pointing on the main road that runs from Kaonik to the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: From Kaonik to Kiseljak, in the direction of Kiseljak. And here [Indicates] you can see an intersection where the main road and the road leading into the centre of town meet, and then also an intersection leading to Tisovac, which was an area with weekend houses. And then 500 metres in the direction of Kiseljak from the intersection is where the Hotel Tisa is located, on the left-hand side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: If you look from the direction going from Kaonik to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And so Kordic shared those headquarters or was in the same headquarters as the other units, military police, special units, HOS --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The SIS, the internal security services, were headed by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The person heading the SIS in Busovaca was Anto Sliskovic, son of Branko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The headquarters remained there, I think, until the arrival of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The headquarters of SIS and the seat of the civilian authority -- that is, the police -- was in the police administration building in Busovaca, and the seat of the SIS and the military police was on the premises of Meraja, which was right behind the bus station. And even today, Anto Sliskovic has his business premises there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did they move to those places after the arrival of UNPROFOR, having been based at the hotel --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No. The police force, both the civilian and military and the SIS, were always there; that is, behind the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And I must just clarify: With which other units, if any, did Kordic share his Hotel Tisa headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: In Hotel Tisa, there were the intervention platoon, and special military police units, and ZNG, and HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I come to the new headquarters for Kordic, I want to ask you about some other particular brigades. First of all, the Zrinjski HVO brigade: Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The Zrinjski Brigade was established towards the end of 1992. It consisted of all units; that is to say the HOS, ZNG, the special military police, the MUP, and the rest of the mobilised population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Second, Skorpions: What can you tell us about the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The Skorpions were part of the intervention platoon. They were the bodyguards of Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What did you see of those bodyguards around the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I saw a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How were they dressed? What arms did they have? What were their apparent duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They, the Skorpions, were Dario Kordic's bodyguards. They guarded him day and night. They were his drivers. They escorted him from one place to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What arms did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They were privileged in terms of weapons; that is to say that they had long-barrelled guns and pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did they have personal body protection as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: From time to time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was that common for Croat soldiers, or was that particular to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They always had this, whereas the other young men wore it as kind of a fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Always wore what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is paragraph 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was concerned with protection, with protective clothing they may have had. What particular protective clothing did they have that others may not have had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Well, they had bullet-proof vests.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. A few personalities, paragraph 17: Who was the commander of the Zrinjski Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The commander was Dusko Grubesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I want you to deal with a few names. Milenko Arapovic, Milijan Kristo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They, Milenko and Milijan, were persons who belonged to the Skorpions, who were bodyguards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did Kordic dress at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I personally saw him in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he wear a badge of rank and any insignia? If so, what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I would see HVO insignia when the HVO was established, and some kind of a rank. I did not find the rank to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think the transcript has got the last name of the -- it's been corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you see something the celebrations concerning the founding of the HVO held in the stadium of Busovaca, paragraph 27?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. Well, since Muslims were not allowed to move freely, there was a curfew from 10.00 until 10.00 the next day. The Muslim population was watching, and they saw what was going on by way of television, through TV Busovaca. I had the opportunity of watching this ceremony on television in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was that celebration shown on television once, or more than once? In any event, what was the nature of the celebration that you saw, and did Kordic say something that you can recall about a Muslim mosque in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The ceremony was recorded. It was recorded by Zoran Jovanovic. It was filmed in its entirety, and it was played publicly every day; that is to say it was repeated several times. As for the mosque and Dario Kordic, he had films shown on television, and on one occasion when he was talking to Zoran Jovanovic, that was in '93, that is, in January, perhaps the 29th, when the conflict in Busovaca broke out, or later, he said -- or rather Zoran asked him, "Well," he said, "our municipality is a Croatian municipality now; we got rid of the Muslims. What do you think about the mosque?" Among other things, Kordic said that there is a mosque in Rome, too, so why shouldn't there be one in Busovaca as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In the event, what happened to the Busovaca mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The Busovaca mosque was mined and torched during 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll maybe return to paragraph 30, press on, and we've dealt with 31 already. Ante Sliskovic, was he well known to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was his relationship with Kordic? By "relationship," I mean relationship in terms of who had authority over who.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Kordic was Ante Sliskovic's superior. Their relationship was a friendly one. Ante Sliskovic's brother, Franjo, got married to the sister of Dario Kordic's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Had Ante Sliskovic been commander of the reserve police forces in 1991 and '92, and did he become the head of the SIS in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to geography in a little more detail. It will help the Court if, with the pointer, and just to remind us, you indicate the main road again running through Busovaca, and just leave the pointer on that junction of the road that leads up to Tisovac. Thank you. At that junction we see a V-junction where, if you were coming from Kiseljak to the south, you could bear left and go into the centre of Busovaca, or you could stay on the main road and continue on to Kaonik; and just into that V-junction, you could turn left up the road towards Tisovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So if the witness may now have and lay on top of the coloured map the first two sheets of the Exhibit 1725, which is -- I hold up my version of these; they actually belong together. They form a composite document, and I'm sorry that they haven't been stuck together in your papers, but one has been prepared in this format, I think, for the witness, or he can have mine. It's only stuck together with paper clips, but if he has this one, it'll be easier. This may be difficult, but if we -- it's going to be easier, if the usher gives it back to me, it will save time. I'm sorry. My mistake. If you would like to lay it --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And if the ELMO could go back a bit. Thank you very much. And then move it a little -- a little to the left, but only a tiny bit to the left. The other way. The right. Right. That's fine. And staying exactly there. Thank you so much. Do we see at the top of this drawing of yours, running right to left, the main road from Kiseljak on the right going towards Kaonik on the left? And do we see where you just put the pointer that same "V" junction that you pointed out on the former map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: [indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you then draw, leading down from that junction, the road that goes to Tisovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: [indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am going to ask you about various features of that map in due course. Before I do so, Your Honours will appreciate that I generally prefer all maps to be oriented to the north and find it difficult to reinterpret them any other way. Doing it this way means that we have to read things upside down. I hope that's not unhelpful. Did you on a day in July 1992 with a companion Arif Delija go to go fishing along that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, but not along that road. We walked along the river. This is the river of Ivancica. Here it is [indicates]. And in the area of Tisovac it touches the road and at other places it goes away from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you come to an area where there is a bridge near a location called Meraja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. That's this part here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. When you got there, did you encounter some soldiers? If so, can you give us the names of any of them and then tell us what they did or said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. Here. Here. See, over here [indicates]. This is the road to Tisovac. So this is Meraja, this is the river of Ivancica. This is the road, only a few houses and then this bridge. That's the way it was. Then this stream. That comes from Orlovaca. See, it flows into the Ivancica. Then there is a bridge, a bridge to cross this little river. Then over here, this is where there was a HVO checkpoint. Here. Right here. This is where a flag was flying, a chequerboard flag [indicates]. We walked along the river. We were fishing. This is about 30 metres away, that is to say the stream is about 30 metres away from the river, and it flows into it. So we were fishing there. And then we came here, here [indicates]. This is the road that leads to the house of -- the house on the other side of the bridge. So there is this small settlement here. This area over here [indicates] is just a field. There is grass. They were sitting there, two men in uniform. One was Spomenko. The other one was Boban. When we came there, there is trout, there is whirlpools, we were surprised and they were surprised. And they said, "You can't go any further. We are securing this area. This is where the HVO headquarters is and we've been ordered not to allow any ethnic Muslims to get in here." So that's how we came there, since they didn't let us go beyond this Meraja. At the checkpoint was Jozo Akrap, Ivica Akrap and, I don't know, some other guys. We knew each other very well, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, if you remember any of the other names of the people at the checkpoint, let me know and give us the names. But these people that you knew, from where did they come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: These people, for example Jozo and Ivica, are brothers. They are from the area of Carica that you can see here on the map. So the local commune of Carica and the municipality of Busovaca. Then this Boban, he's from the local commune of Juriceve Bare.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The name Boban, is that a first name or a last name, and do you know any other part of his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Boban is his real name. At school we called him Bobi, though. And the other one was Vrhovac. His house was here on the other side when you cross the little bridge [indicates]. He wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I am going to stop you for a minute. Are we going to be assisted with quite all this detail?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Names may be material because, of course, records may turn up later and issues may be in dispute. But I've got as far as I want with those names and I was going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice, I think that all this is all right for the background, but I think we should go a little faster, because, after all, it's almost 50 minutes now since we started with this testimony, and we are still in the preliminary stage. So I do think that we should speed things up a little. Even if it is necessary, it can be done more speedily.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, I am very much in the hands of the manner of delivery of the witness, and I'm not going to lead unless I am allowed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 39. These soldiers who barred your progress, were they armed? Just "yes" or "no" to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they had long weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Croat headquarters itself, is that shown on your plan? If so, point it out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: [Indicates] Yes. When the U.N. forces came to the area of the municipality of Busovaca, they took the Tisa hotel premises. The military structures of the HVO government that were organised by the HDZ were relocated and brought to Tisovac --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: -- by the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you barred from approaching that headquarters by these soldiers, and did you decide to press on up the river towards the Grad Mountain Lodge? Just "yes" or "no" will do for this. But before leaving the checkpoint, did you notice something in the ground, and if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. When crossing from the river to the checkpoint, we passed by some buried bodies. That's over here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did you know they were buried bodies there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Parts of their fingers could be seen. They were sticking out of the ground. And also parts of their legs, feet. Through the conversation --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, carry on. Did one of the soldiers tell you something about these bodies? If so, which soldier and what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He said -- Boban said that these were some imprisoned Serb soldiers, that they were taken somewhere by Kotor Vares and that they were executed over here. We talked there and they did not let us pass any further. They could not guarantee our safety by the Ivancica river. We asked for them to let us pass at our own responsibility. And we were not supposed to tell anyone. If anyone were to stop us later by the river, that they had let us get through. We went on fishing. We proceeded there towards the Vatrostalna villa. You cannot see it there. And also there was a fish pond for raising Californian trout, and we reached the Busovaca waterworks. This is the main station for providing drinking water to the town. We were stopped there by the soldiers. We were surrounded. We heard them and we were also at a lower point. Among others, Arapovic, Milenko Arapovic walked up to us. He ordered us to put our fishing tackle down and to raise our hands. And they were cussing at us. They said that we were extremists who were sent to sabotage the headquarters, et cetera. We did not want to drop our fishing tackle at that point and he uncocked his pistol, 765, and he shot above our heads. Then he -- then we realised that he was not joking. And we dropped our tackle and raised our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you taken to the so-called fish farm, and since this is a feature in the ground which can be proved, I hope, by a photograph, is that a series of concrete structures built for the breeding of Californian trout to serve the hotel restaurant before the war? Paragraph 50.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they escorted us with weapons to the fish pond and they insulted us. They abused us verbally. They insisted that we strip down to our underwear so that they could search us. We refused to do that. We did not know the reason for that. And we did not know of any reason why they should mistreat us. So we were quarrelling with him. "Who are you? Fishing Lasva, which river is ours," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers present there whom you can name? If so, just give us the names? If you can't name anybody at the moment, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There were five or six soldiers there. One of them was Herman Lastro. I think his surname was Lastro. The other one was Boban Lastro. The third was Zarko Goran or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: All right. The fish ponds themselves, did they have covers over the top of them, metal covers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No. The ponds were made out of reinforced concrete and they were linked in threes. They had a two-metre wire fence around them on the outside. They didn't have nets covering them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Were they visible from the headquarters building which you've already indicated and which I'd like you to name? Could you see that headquarters building from the fish pond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The HVO headquarters, or rather the think tank, was in the Ivancica villa, and the ponds were further up. The ponds were here [indicates], and only the trees could be seen above the ponds, because they are in a valley. So it was not possible to directly see the pond itself, or the water in the pond. But above the fence, from the balcony of the villa, one could see the treetops.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: And the small hut that had been left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In the event, were you released from the control of these soldiers because a man called Nikica Grubesic, who knew you, came by and ordered your release?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. Just then, we thought that we would be executed in the course of this argument. We were unaware where we were going. We didn't know that the headquarters was there. They kept repeating to us that the headquarters was there, and that we had been infiltrated there by the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Whose headquarters was it that was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: At the time, this was the headquarters of the HVO of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And do you know where Kordic was? Was this Kordic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: He would come occasionally to those headquarters, though his -- I don't think he was there permanently, but he was present. I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the witness see, please, the exhibit that is a rather poor photograph at the end of the exhibit? It's 2703. Just lay it on top of the existing maps because we may return to the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The background to this photograph, which we're just losing, includes a flag -- if the technical booth could just go out -- that's fine. We can see a background of trees. Are you able to help at all with the location or possible location of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I think -- I believe this photograph was taken in the environs of the Ivancica villa, the Tisovac villa. This flag, these flags, or flags like this, were present on all roads. At the entrance to Tisovac, at command posts, everywhere where there was a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And the trees behind the defendant, does that accord with the general area of Tisovac? Is that a wooded area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Behind the villa, yes, there is a wooded pine wood, or a mixed wood, with oak and pine trees, behind the villa, going from Busovaca towards the villa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Having been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a normal objection, but as the Prosecutor is tendering this photograph through this witness, perhaps it would be useful for us to ask when this photograph was taken and where it was published.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The photograph, I'm afraid, has to speak for itself, insofar as it can't be the subject of evidence. It's -- the identity of the subject is clear. I'm at the moment attempting to establish its likely location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Mr. Naumovski, we are professional judges; we're not a jury. Now, what is the next point? This photograph, we've heard the evidence. If you want to ask the witness about it, you can. Now, what can your objection be?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: It is that the witness has been shown a photograph that we know nothing about, and he is not the author of that photograph, and how can the witness recognise it when it is not a clear photograph anyway? So that is our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We understand that. If you are objecting to the admissibility of the evidence, it is admissible. As to its weight, we will have to determine what weight it has. We have heard what the witness has said about it, and we can see the photographs. We can make up our own minds. There should be a broad approach to admissibility. As to weight, well, we'll have to decide whether we think it's got any weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Having been saved by the man Grubesic, were you returned to the checkpoint in Meraja and able to go home in due course? Just "yes" to that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The photograph and the hand-drawn map can be removed, leaving the coloured map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there an occasion at the end of July 1992 when you and your companion, same companion, had been on Mount Busovaca -- I think you were a mountaineer and things like that -- and did you come to a place in the Peska forestry work site north of Busovaca by some 12 to 15 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you there hear some noises which led to your hiding behind some trees, in due course to see some HVO soldiers whom or some of whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, you're pointing at something that is southwest of Busovaca, so if what I've put is incorrect about the place being to the north of Busovaca, you must correct me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is above Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case the summary is wrong. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: First of all, name, please, the soldiers whom you are able to name, and then we'll ask you for a quick summary of what it is that you saw them do. Names of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Among them were Zoran Marinic; a Petrovic; Zeljo Vukadinovic; Miro Petrovic; Nedeljko Glibo, Akrap, who used to work in Sumarstvo, forestry administration; Mile, who used to drive a three-barrelled gun --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: -- and a --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did they have with them a prisoner Serb soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, a man most probably of Serb ethnic origin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you can take this evidence shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've read it. I don't know that it's going to assist very much, although of course it was an important incident at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. I'm much obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there a freshly dug grave? Had the man's ears been cut off? Was he moaning and asking the soldiers to put an end to his suffering? Did he get killed in circumstances which you were not able to see directly, and after he was killed, did one of those soldiers say something to the other soldiers about how a real Ustasha does it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. We were on our way back from the Crni Vrh, or Black Peak --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to have to interrupt you, Witness T, but you'll understand that time is limited, and where questions can be dealt with by a yes or no, that's, I'm afraid, the way we have to deal with it. Did you also hear a rifle, it appeared the Kalashnikov you had seen, being fired? Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I did hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Although -- and just for the completeness of the picture and to help my learned friends opposite, you didn't see the killing, and you've seen your statement to the Bosnian authorities, and you can't explain the detail that's provided in that statement apparently taken from you; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. We saw the event up to the killing, and the actual killing was something we couldn't see because this three-barrelled gun appeared behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. And then I think we can look very briefly at the exhibit, the next part of the same drawings exhibit, which is a sheet with the number 00685930 on it, and just identify this is the drawing that shows the location. Just confirm, please, that this shows your drawing of the event. The various terms have not been translated into English. Can you just point out with the pointer where it was in relation to the other features shown on the plan that the killing occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: This is the road to Rovna, and here it branches off to the left about 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Did the soldiers drive away in the direction of the Peska forestry enterprise in a vehicle that was ex-JNA and painted in camouflage with "ZNG" marked on the doors in white letters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you return to the area later, and were you given some information from a man called Ivan Petrovic, of the community of Ravan, about the capture and killing of Serb soldiers in Ravan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, but they didn't speak of one man and they didn't mention the location Peska, but they spoke of a number of killings in the area of Tisovac, killings of Serbs, people, or rather soldiers that were captured in the area of Skender Vakuf, Kotor Varos, Jajce; somewhere there, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I shan't read the names of the two informant companions or acquaintances, in the interests of their safety. They are given at paragraph 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In August '92, was the Busovaca Territorial Defence disbanded along with a mixed military force, and at that stage, did you notice anything of people from outside Herceg-Bosna in the area of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence operated up to the 25th of January 1993. As far as the authorities permitted as they supervised -- they were supervised by representatives of the HDZ and by military authorities, the command of the Territorial Defence was disbanded in the town centre and it was transferred to the area of Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's turn then to the presence of outsiders in your town --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let's, in fact, call it a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I notice that you are coming up to paragraph 70. That would not seem to me admissible. I don't know whether you thought of leading it, but it seems to me something of a view of that kind, an opinion of that sort is not a matter for the witness. What he can tell us is what he knows about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I.e., what he saw and heard, rather than what he believes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. But his proximity to an eyewitness follows in the subsequent paragraphs, but of course his belief has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, the evidence about facts is one thing, but unless it can be substantiated in some way, it's not evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: His belief is neither here nor there. But he may be able to tell us what somebody else said, if that person is sufficiently approximate to the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the witness is being slower than any of us would have wished, but we all have different ways of delivery. And I'll try and make assumptions about my rights to lead without offending the defence a little more tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness, of course, is not to be criticised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Unless there are any other matters, we'll adjourn. Witness T, could you come back, please, tomorrow morning at half past nine to go on with your evidence. Would you please remember in this adjournment and any others there may be not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over. And that, of course, includes the members of the Prosecution. Half past nine tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: p.m. to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of November, 1999 at 9.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
